title: Capstone submission checklist
idea: A final submission is a package someone else can verify without you: requirements, diagrams, runnable code, passing checks and a record of your decisions.
points: A stranger runs every check using the `javac` and `java` lines in your README.
Diagrams must match the code: same class names, same `book` and `cancel` signatures.
The decision log explains each trade-off and each declined review comment.
List known limits honestly, such as no recurring meetings and in-memory storage.

hero.title: What goes in the package
head: Item
Contents
Done when
rows: Each rule traces to a class or check
Class and sequence diagrams as Mermaid text
Compiles and runs with the JDK only
Happy path plus each error code
Every feedback id has an outcome
What this version does not do
Written down, not discovered by a reviewer
hero.caption: Read the Done when column as your final test. Any row you cannot tick is not finished.

pitfalls: Submitting diagrams drawn before the last refactor; reviewers spot renamed classes at once.
Shipping only happy-path checks; include `ROOM_TAKEN`, `INVALID_SLOT` and `NOT_OWNER` cases.

quiz.q: Your class diagram shows `reserve`, but the code says `book`. What should you do before submitting?
options: Leave it; reviewers read the code, not the diagram
Add a note saying the names differ
Update the diagram so it matches the code
quiz.why: The diagram documents the code that ships. Diagrams-as-code are cheap to edit, while a last-minute rename risks breaking checks and callers.

takeaway: Submit a package a stranger can run, read and trust.

starters: Can you review my submission list for the booking system and spot gaps?
How detailed should my known limits section be?
What would I change if the booking system had to persist to a database next?
